paper_id: Urban Traffic Accident Risk Prediction Revisited_ Regionality, Proximity, Similarity and Sparsity
title: Urban Traffic Accident Risk Prediction Revisited: Regionality, Proximity, Similarity and Sparsity
motivation: UN target halving road deaths by 2030; existing methods fail to capture regional background, spatial-semantic correlations, and zero-inflation sparsity
key_insight: Remote sensing images reveal regional background inaccessible to POI; multi-level hierarchy addresses sparsity by aggregating to coarser granularity
method_signature: MGHSTN: remote sensing autoencoder + multi-level region/graph hierarchy + cross-level message passing + adaptive temporal attention + multivariate loss
evaluation_criteria: RMSE, Recall, MAP across NYC and Chicago datasets; ablation validates each component's contribution
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Remote sensing improvement more obvious for Chicago where POI data is sparse, suggesting RS acts as data substitute not enrichment
evidence_for_taste: often overlooked and difficult to capture
thinking_moves: 把regional background视为隐变量,用遥感图像替代稀缺POI来捕获
稀疏问题不是硬预测而是层次聚合降维
语义相似度用JS散度量化,物理proximity用卷积捕获,分离两种相关性
多级预测任务作为辅助loss约束,隐式缓解零膨胀
